title: Checkpoint 1 — Intro & Hardware
description: Quick check after the home automation intro and hardware tour.

questions.prompt: Almost every home automation gadget follows the same three-step pattern. What is it?
questions.explanation: Read something (sensor), decide what to do (logic), then make something happen (output).

questions.prompt: In today's project, which part is the "brain" that runs the logic?
questions.explanation: The ESP32 microcontroller runs your code and decides what color to show.

questions.prompt: The DHT22 in our build is an example of a...
questions.explanation: The DHT22 measures temperature and humidity — it's our sensor.

questions.prompt: How is a microcontroller like the ESP32 different from a laptop?
choices: It runs one program at a time and has no operating system
It needs a monitor and keyboard to work
questions.explanation: A microcontroller is tiny, cheap, and built to read sensors and control pins — no screen or OS needed.

questions.prompt: The little LED already built onto the ESP32 board is wired to which pin?
questions.explanation: The onboard LED is on GPIO 2 — perfect for a first test with no wiring.
